# War in Ukraine: Kyiv strikes key Russian supply lines

Russian troops rely on supplies via the land corridor to Crimea, but Ukrainian forces are now able to launch concentrated attacks along the critical route. Experts say this indicates growing Russian vulnerability.

![A military traffic police officer reroutes a truck on a highway]( "A military traffic police officer reroutes a truck on a highway")

Ukrainian forces are fighting for control over the Russian army's key supply routes in the occupied territories of [Ukraine](/en/ukraine/t-17295382). According to Ukrainian military officials, newly developed medium-range weapons are now reaching [Russia's](/en/russia/t-19065060) logistics routes beyond front lines.

Ukrainian [drones](/en/drones/t-38577815) were reportedly conducting surveillance and attacks in the area around Mariupol. That would mean that sections of the land corridor connecting Russan-occupied Ukrainian territory with the [Crimean penninsula](/en/crimea/t-17476118), some 160 kilometers (99 miles) away, are now under fire control. As proof, the Ukrainian military has published numerous online videos purpotedly showing burned-out Russian military vehicles along the road leading through [occupied territories](/en/crimea-russian-military-plane-crash-kills-at-least-29-people/a-76620125) in southern mainland Ukraine to Crimea.

![Vijay Kumar Malesu](https://www.azonetwork.com/themes/clients/images/team/Photo_Vijay-2.jpg)

***As climate shocks, conflict, and trade disruptions threaten the world’s staple crops, a new review maps the policies and technologies that could help vulnerable nations keep food supplies moving.***

![](https://www.news-medical.net/images/news/ImageForNews_839739_17810613913174558.jpg)

![](https://www.news-medical.net/images/news/ImageForNews_839739_17810613913174558.jpg)

## Background

Maize, rice, and wheat are staple foods for billions of people, but rising food prices, climate-related disasters, pandemics, and geopolitical conflicts have made access to these staples increasingly uncertain.

# Two Vessels Under Panama, Barbados Flags Damaged in Attack in Ukrainian Waters

![LOGO](https://www.marinelink.com/Content/MarineLinkLogo.png)

June 10, 2026

![© Adobe Stock/@Zaetaflow](https://images.marinelink.com/images/maritime/w400/adobe-stockzaetaflow-171344.jpeg)

© Adobe Stock/@Zaetaflow

Two vessels under Panamanian and Barbadian flags were damaged after being attacked while moving through Ukraine's Black Sea navigation corridor, the Ukrainian Ports Authority said on Wednesday.

The authority, writing on Telegram, said one vessel was headed for the port of Odesa, critical to Ukrainian exports, with a cargo of metal, while the second was carrying grain and had left the port.

Both were operating within the navigation corridor set up by Ukrainian authorities intended to allow ships to travel through the Black Sea to Romanian ports on the Danube River.

The governor of Odesa region, Oleh Kiper, said on Telegram that Russian drones had carried out the attacks. The Russian defence ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
